answer: An agent economy can resist Sybils with graduated trust: a new identity starts at the vertex of the network with almost no influence, and earns weight only through sustained, verified useful work over time, like slowly climbing toward the zenith of an atlas of reputation. Influence decays when an identity goes idle, so parked accounts lose power. An attacker must therefore fund and operate every fake identity continuously for months to gain real sway, while a single honest agent pays that cost only once, making a large fake swarm prohibitively expensive in time, compute, and upkeep.
